name: T-0013
markdown:

- `tools.check` returns, per tool: found/missing, version string (display only), required/optional, login status for gh/az, the `azure-devops` extension status, and the install command for macOS (e.g. `brew install gh`)
- the permission-mode check reads the user's Claude Code settings files **read-only** and reports "prompting" vs "not prompting"; unreadable or unknown → "unknown" (no warning)
- no code path installs, updates or version-gates a tool
- tests: detection with a fake `PATH` containing stub scripts named `git`/`gh` (ordinary scripts, not a fake claude session); settings parsing from fixture files
- checks green (`scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests); commit names SET-02, PLT-03 and decisions 0021, 0017, 0011, 0016

Claude Code docs; name the source in the PR. Windows/Linux install commands come in T-0159.

name: T-0025
markdown:
Groups are containers and delivery units (d0059). This ticket covers their bookkeeping in `crewboard-core`: **Add ticket to group**
creates a child (SHOP-40.1, 40.2…); **Move to group** is allowed only for a ticket that **never went to Dev**, gives it the group's
next child key (SHOP-51 → SHOP-40.4), adopts the group's branch, and keeps the **old key as an alias** that resolves everywhere
(d0044); **progress** "2 / 3 merged"; and the **close-group plan**: the list of unfinished children to close and agents to stop,
used by the single confirmation (EPC-06). Merged children stay merged. A child can't move to another group.

## Done when

- add child: key `SHOP-40.<next>`, base = group's branch (read-only), no External ID
- move to group: refused if the ticket has ever started, is an group, or is already a child; on success the key changes, a `ticket_key_aliases` row keeps `SHOP-51`, and key lookup by `SHOP-51` returns the moved ticket
- move to group refuses when the ticket's dependencies would cross bases after adopting the group's branch (DEP-02 message)
- `group.progress` returns merged / total children; `group.close_plan` lists unfinished children and which have a running agent
- `group.close` (bookkeeping part) closes the listed children and the group; merged children unchanged; an group with nothing merged ends "Closed · not merged" (d0044)
- tests: unit tests with SHOP-40 Wishlist and children 40.1 (Merged), 40.2 (working, simulated state), 40.3 (Backlog); move SHOP-51 → SHOP-40.4 and resolve the alias
- checks green (`scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests); commit names EPC-01, EPC-06, EPC-07, TKT-07 and decisions 0039, 0044, 0059

**Notes:** stopping agents and removing worktrees on close is wired in T-0100 (M6). The group's integration branch is created in
T-0048 (M3). Follow decision 0033 for worktrees on close (questions Q4, resolved: 0033 wins; the dialog text is fixed by design update H).

name: T-0031

title in tooltip), status pill, orange border + callout for needs-you states, meta row (dependency badges, last signal, tokens,
port, PR chip), hover quick actions, and selected / focused / hovered / dragging / chain-highlighted / dimmed states. Implement
the **flag priority** from the frame as a tested view-model function: one pill, one callout; the highest flag takes the pill, lower
flags fall back to the meta row; **pinned is not a status** and never takes the pill.

## Done when

- a `CardViewModel::from(ticket, flags, now)` maps every status and flag in SDD §7.2 to pill / callout / meta row per *Which flag wins the pill slot*
- the pill is empty when the status equals the column's base status (frame header rule)
- the component renders every variant shown in *Variant grid* from fixture data, in light and dark; compact density per *Compact density*
- long titles truncate after 2 lines with the full title on hover
- variants whose data arrives later (orange family M4, Queued reasons M5, review flags M6, usage M8, Run M9, PR M10) render from fixtures now and light up as their tickets land
- tests: unit tests for the priority function (e.g. Needs you + Running + 2 deps → Needs you pill, `▶ :4020` and `⛓` in the meta row); checked by hand against *04 · Ticket card variants* Light and Dark
- checks green (`scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests); commit names UI-03 and decisions 0047, 0042, 0027, 0020

**Notes:** use the sample tickets (SHOP-17…SHOP-28, BILL-4) as fixtures. The "asked SHOP-40.1 · waiting" flag (MSG-06) is added to the

name: T-0048
markdown:
Each ticket works in its own git worktree **outside the user's repo**, at `~/.crewboard/wt/<repo-name>/<KEY>` (d0010, d0023), on
a **temporary branch** `crewboard/<KEY>` (GIT-07, d0050; the real name is chosen at the first push in M10). Resolve the base
first (SES-01 step 1): standalone tickets and groups use their base branch; **group children use the group's branch**, which is
created on the first child's start as `crewboard/SHOP-40` from the group's base (EPC-02). Record `base_sha` (where the ticket left
its base). Everything must be **idempotent** (SES-02): re-running reuses an existing worktree or branch.

## Done when

- `prepare_worktree(ticket)` resolves the base (ticket base, or the group's branch for SHOP-40.2), creates `crewboard/<KEY>` from it and adds the worktree at `~/.crewboard/wt/shop-web/SHOP-18`
- the first child start of an group creates `crewboard/SHOP-40` from the group's base; later children reuse it; the group gets no agent and no worktree of its own
- `base_sha`, `branch_name` and `worktree_path` are stored on the ticket; the base branch becomes locked once started (`branch_locked`)
- re-running after any partial state (branch exists, worktree exists, worktree folder missing but registered) converges to the same result without errors
- nothing is written inside the user's repo folder other than git's own worktree metadata under `.git/`
- tests: temp git repos — fresh start, re-run, partial states, group child creating then reusing the group branch, `SHOP-40.1` key in paths
- checks green (`scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests); commit names SES-01, SES-02, EPC-02, GIT-07 and decisions 0010, 0023, 0029, 0050, 0059

**Notes:** merges into the group branch run in a Crewboard-owned scratch worktree (T-0089); this ticket only creates the branch.

name: T-0054
markdown:
Crewboard types into live sessions in two ways (d0048). **Automatic deliveries** (another agent's question or answer, the
ticket-change note, "continue" after the limit reset) are stored in `pending_deliveries` and sent **only when the agent is idle
between turns and the input line is empty** (SES-06); until then the ticket shows **"1 message waiting · Deliver now"**. **The
user's own clicks** (Send back, an inbox answer) are never held: if the line has unsent text, the request returns a prompt —
*"SHOP-23 has unsent text in its terminal"* → **Keep it and cancel** / **Clear it and send** (SES-07). Crewboard **never clears the
user's text silently**. The "idle between turns" predicate comes from hook signals (T-0066/T-0067); here it is an injected input.

## Done when

- `queue_delivery(session, kind, text)` stores a pending delivery and emits a card-status event with the waiting count
- pending deliveries are sent in order the moment the session is idle **and** the unsent flag is clear; each is typed then submitted, and removed from the queue
- **Deliver now** (user click) sends immediately if the line is empty; if it has unsent text it returns the Keep/Clear prompt instead
- `deliver_from_click(session, text)` returns `NeedsConfirmation { ticket }` when unsent text exists; `clear_and_send` clears the line (resetting the flag) then sends; `keep` sends nothing
- tests: unit tests with an injected idle predicate and unsent flag covering: held while busy, held while unsent text, delivered when both clear, Deliver now, Keep/Clear outcomes; PTY test with `cat`
- checks green (`scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests); commit names SES-06, SES-07 and decision 0048

**Notes:** the restack note from d0048 is deferred with stacking (d0049); don't build it.

name: T-0066
markdown:
`crewboard hook <event>` (in `crewboard-cli`) is what the plugin's hooks call. It reads the hook JSON from stdin and **does
nothing when `CREWBOARD_TICKET` is unset** (PLG-04), so the user's ordinary `claude` sessions are unaffected. The service maps
events per SDD §11.4: `Notification` with `permission_prompt`, `elicitation_dialog`, `elicitation_url_dialog` or
`agent_needs_input` → **Needs you** (other types ignored); `Stop` with non-empty `background_tasks` or `session_crons` → **Working
in background** with what it waits for; `Stop` with both empty and no `review submit` / `ask human` this turn → **Idle**;
`UserPromptSubmit` → back to working. Every hook updates the **last signal**. `StopFailure` is logged only; acting on it
(Waiting for limit reset) is T-0128 in M8.

## Done when

- `crewboard hook Notification|Stop|StopFailure|UserPromptSubmit` exits 0 quickly and silently when `CREWBOARD_TICKET` is unset, and never blocks the agent if the service is unreachable
- the mapping above is a pure function from (event, payload, turn facts) to a signal, with the background summary text ("background: test run, 1 helper agent · 6 min", "wakes up at 4:10pm")
- the service tracks per turn whether `review submit` or `ask human` ran, reset on `UserPromptSubmit`
- raw payloads are logged (debug level) so undocumented fields can be verified against real sessions
- tests: feed `crewboard hook <event>` real-shaped JSON for every row of §11.4 (incl. a permission prompt inside a helper agent and `idle_prompt` ignored); unset `CREWBOARD_TICKET` → no-op
- checks green (`scripts/check.sh`: fmt, clippy -D warnings, tests); commit names PLG-04, ATT-01, ATT-04 and decisions 0009, 0042, 0020

**Notes:** payload fields beyond the documented ones must be verified by logging real payloads (d0020, d0042, SDD §26); name
the Claude Code version checked in the PR.

name: T-0089
markdown:
Local merge is the user's approve action that needs no tokens (d0015, d0038). On the click, in a **Crewboard-owned scratch
worktree** (never the user's folder): (1) refuse if the ticket's worktree has **uncommitted files** ("SHOP-19 has 2 uncommitted
files", REV-08); (2) update the target — for a base branch: fetch, fast-forward if only behind, refuse if diverged (GIT-01); an
group branch is local only; (3) **free rebase** of the ticket branch onto the latest target (checkpoint rule, T-0088); (4) clean →
**squash-merge** with the confirmed message; if the target is checked out in the user's folder and that checkout is **clean**,
fast-forward it; if it has **uncommitted changes**, refuse: "shop-web has uncommitted changes on main. Clean up and retry."; (5)
conflict → nothing is merged, the ticket stays in Ready for Review with **Send to agent to fix** (T-0090). Group children merge into
the **group branch** (EPC-03). **Local merge never pushes.** On success the ticket becomes Done · Merged.

## Done when

- `ticket.local_merge(key, squash_message)` implements steps 1–5 in order and returns `Merged`, `RefusedUncommitted{files}`, `RefusedDiverged`, `RefusedDirtyCheckout`, or `Conflict`
- a proposed squash message (ticket key + title + agent summary) is available before the click and is editable by the caller
- the scratch worktree lives under `~/.crewboard/` and is reused/cleaned by Crewboard; the user's checkout is only ever fast-forwarded, and only when clean

- group children target the group's branch (created in T-0048); standalone tickets and groups target their base branch

resolve that first with the `restack` skill. Implement this in `crewboard-core`.
